The '''2013–14 Scottish Premiership''' was the first season of the [[Scottish Premiership]], the highest division of [[Football in Scotland|Scottish football]].<ref name = "premiership">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23435136 |title=SPFL: New Scottish league brands unveiled |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=24 July 2013 |access-date=24 July 2013}}</ref> The season began on 2 August 2013 and concluded on 11 May 2014.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scotprem.com/content/default.asp?page=s49 | title=Key dates | publisher=Scottish Premier League | access-date=18 June 2013 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130705063057/http://www.scotprem.com/content/default.asp?page=s49 | archive-date=5 July 2013}}</ref> This was the first season of the competition being part of the newly formed [[Scottish Professional Football League]] after the merger of the [[Scottish Premier League]] and the [[Scottish Football League]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22864944 | title=SFL clubs vote in favour of merger with SPL | publisher=BBC | date=12 June 2013 | access-date=18 June 2013}}</ref> This season also featured the introduction of an end of season play-off between the 11th-placed team in the top flight and the teams placed 2nd–4th in the [[Scottish Championship]], to determine whether a second team will be relegated from the league.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/jun/12/scottish-football-league-scottish-premier-league | title=Scottish Football League 'swallowed up' by Scottish Premier League | work=The Guardian| date=12 June 2013 | agency=Press Association | access-date=18 June 2013}}</ref>

Twelve teams contested the league. [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] (champions) were promoted from the [[2012–13 Scottish First Division|2012–13 First Division]], replacing [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] (relegated). [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] were deducted 15 points (one-third of the previous season's total) for entering [[administration (British football)|administration]] during the close season.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22944291 | title=Hearts: SPL side to enter administration | publisher=BBC | work=BBC Sport | date=17 June 2013 | access-date=17 June 2013 | author=McLauchlin, Brian}}</ref>

On 26 March, Celtic clinched their third title in a row and 45th in total after a 5–1 away win against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/mar/26/celtic-partick-thistle-scottish-premier-league-match-report|title=Celtic crush Partick Thistle to make it three SPL titles in a row|date=26 March 2014|work=The Guardian|access-date=26 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/celtic/10724728/Partick-Thistle-1-Celtic-5-match-report.html|title=Partick Thistle 1 Celtic 5|date=26 March 2014|work=The Daily Telegraph|access-date=26 March 2014}}</ref>
It is the earliest that the title has been won since the [[1928–29 Scottish Division One|1928–29]] season, when Rangers won it on 16 March,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/celtic-title-1383544-Mar2014/|title=Stokes leads the way as five-goal Celtic win 45th Scottish title|date=26 March 2014|work=The Score|access-date=26 March 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327234236/http://www.thescore.ie/celtic-title-1383544-Mar2014/|archive-date=27 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/celtic-make-it-three-titles-in-a-row-with-victory-over-partick-thistle-30129170.html|title=Celtic make it three titles in a row with victory over Partick Thistle|date=26 March 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=26 March 2014}}</ref> until the [[2020–21 Scottish Premiership|2020–21]] Season when Rangers won the title on 7 March.

==Season statistics==
[[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] goalkeeper [[Fraser Forster]] set a new Scottish league record for length of time played without conceding a goal, which had been previously set by [[Bobby Clark (footballer, born 1945)|Bobby Clark]] in [[1970–71 in Scottish football|1970–71]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26306540 |title=Fraser Forster: Celtic clean sheet record a team effort |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=22 February 2014 |access-date=22 February 2014}}</ref> Forster's streak ended at 1,256 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25892139 |title=Aberdeen 2–1 Celtic |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=25 February 2014 |access-date=25 February 2014}}</ref>

==Premiership play-offs==
For the first time since the [[1996–97 Scottish Premier Division|1996–97]] season, [[promotion and relegation]] involving a place in the top division of the [[Scottish football league system]] was determined in part by a play-off system.<ref name = "playoffs">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22353579 |title=Scottish Premier League considers play-off introduction |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |first=Andy |last=Campbell |date=30 April 2013 |access-date=11 December 2013}}</ref> The previous system used was a straight head-to-head between the team that had finished 9th (second bottom) in the [[Scottish Football League Premier Division|Premier Division]] and the runner-up in the [[Scottish Football League First Division|First Division]].<ref name = "playoffs"/> The new system involved the teams from second to fourth place in the [[Scottish Championship|Championship]], with the first contest between the third and fourth place teams.<ref name="schedule">{{cite web |url=http://spfl.co.uk/play-offs/ |title=Play-offs |work=spfl.co.uk |publisher=Scottish Professional Football League |access-date=28 December 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131225065839/http://spfl.co.uk/play-offs/ |archive-date=25 December 2013}}</ref> The winner progressed to a tie with the second place Championship team.<ref name = "schedule"/> The winner of that second tie then progressed to the promotion and relegation deciding playoff against the 11th place team in the Premiership.<ref name = "schedule"/>
